subject: HANDOFF: Shizuku privilege/daemon recovery fence
body: WORKSTREAM_ID=reviewer-shizuku-recovery-gen2-20261001. R&D complete against unchanged main 45bb0d326899c0e08415928224cfea0ff58d2d4e. Strongest source-confirmed finding: privilege loss invalidates app-side cover readiness/authority but does not demote Fold7ContinuityController out of COVER_READY_HIDDEN/COVER_VISUAL or necessarily revoke mirrorRequested; therefore a later hinge sample can request COVER_VISUAL from stale READY_HIDDEN state without fresh route proof. visualMirrorActive also lacks a privilege/readiness term. Second source-confirmed finding: DuoShellService SHIZUKU_DESTROY explicitly stops the live mirror but shuts the cover mutation executor and exits without draining/reconciling Fold7CoverPanelLease; the existing Fold7CoverPanelLease.onPrivilegedDaemonRestart() recovery hook is not integrated into the inspected startup/reconcile path. A 9/9 isolated adversarial model reproduces the app-side authority divergence and validates a Gen2 recovery fence. Recommended integration: treat Shizuku connection/shell lifetime as an authority epoch; on loss revoke local visual authority and mark privileged close state recovery-required; on reconnect run recovery before trusting prior READY/VISUAL state and require fresh readiness before ShowMirror. On graceful shell destroy, serially drain the exact known cover lease using validated logical reset semantics; on cold shell start, gate new prewarm behind UNKNOWN_RECOVERY resolution rather than treating unknown ownership as clean IDLE. Never issue raw physical OFF. Strongest remaining uncertainty: whether the Fold7 physical/logical cover mutation persists after abrupt UserService death on the actual device; this is a device-validation requirement, not claimed as confirmed. No production GitHub writes were performed. Manual primary integration review is required. Latest state-rd work on close-cycle prime/capture arbitration was reconciled and is complementary, not duplicate.
